claim.qualifier: Lucid's brand language emphasizes engineering excellence, range leadership, and luxury craftsmanship at $100K+ price point.
claim.verbatim_quote: Meticulously engineered for the luxury performance segment

reality.qualifier: 5 NHTSA recalls active for 2025 Lucid Air: rear motor / electrical propulsion system (24V836000), driveshaft (25V669000 and 26V193000 — two separate driveshaft campaigns), backup camera software (25V670000 and 26V017000 — two separate camera-software campaigns).
reality.verbatim_quote: Lucid USA, Inc. is recalling certain 2024-2025 Air Pure rear wheel drive vehicles. [Multiple recalls including rear electrical propulsion, driveshaft (twice), backup camera software (twice).]

narrative_one_liner: Lucid Air 2025: 5 NHTSA recalls — including TWO driveshaft and TWO backup-camera campaigns. At $100K+ this is notable.
narrative: The Lucid Air 2025 is subject to 5 NHTSA recalls. Notable: two separate driveshaft recall campaigns (25V669000 and 26V193000) — having to issue a second driveshaft recall after the first suggests the original remedy was incomplete, a quality-process concern. Similarly, two separate backup camera software recalls. Lucid markets the Air at $100K+ with 'meticulously engineered' luxury positioning. The recall pattern does not match this positioning.
methodology_notes: Tier-1 NHTSA data. The pattern of repeated recalls on the same component (driveshaft, backup camera) is a stronger signal than total count alone — it indicates defect-remediation incompleteness.
caveats: Some campaigns affect only Air Pure RWD (the lowest-cost trim, not the Grand Touring documented in our product file). The product-record applies to GT trim; recall applicability needs per-VIN verification.
Lucid is a small manufacturer; absolute recall counts are smaller than mass-market vehicles by raw VIN volume.
Severity 'moderate' rather than 'high' because none of the recalls are battery or steering safety-critical at the level of Rivian's pattern.
alternative_explanations: Lucid's small fleet means each defect produces a recall earlier than at higher-volume manufacturers (lower threshold to surface).
Repeated driveshaft and backup camera recalls may reflect supplier issues rather than Lucid engineering — but this is invisible to consumers.
